'''Decipher.com''' was the official website of [[Decipher]], the publisher of the [[Star Wars CCG|Star Wars Customizable Card Game]]. It went online in 1996 and carried news, rules, card lists, contests, tournament information, message boards and mailing lists for Decipher's games. The ''Star Wars CCG'' section stopped changing after Decipher's license ended on 31 December 2001 and stayed online as an archive until about 2008. From 2005 the address forwarded to other Decipher sites, and since 2014 it has shown a single page about ''How to Host a Murder''.

== History ==
=== 1996–1999: the lobby ===
The earliest archived copy of the site is from 2 November 1996, on the host games.decipher.com; www.decipher.com was first archived on 21 November 1996.<ref name="splash1996">[http://www.decipher.com/ Welcome to Decipher Inc.], Decipher (November 1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961121225926/http://www.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref> The first page was a splash screen with the slogan "The Art of Great Games", recommending Netscape Navigator and plug-ins for animation and video.

Behind the splash page was a "lobby" with image-map navigation. It led to six areas: The Galleries, Star Wars Customizable Cards, Star Trek:TNG Customizable Cards, Decipher Shop, Inside Decipher and Decipher's West Wing.<ref name="lobby1996">[http://games.decipher.com/index.html Welcome To Decipher!], Decipher (December 1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961231210635/http://games.decipher.com/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> The West Wing covered Decipher's party games and was renamed the East Wing by June 1997.<ref name="eastwing">[http://www.decipher.com/eastwing/index.html Welcome To Decipher's East Wing!], Decipher (June 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970607091652/http://www.decipher.com/eastwing/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> In 1998 the lobby added a Welcome Center, search, help, a "new" page and a Question of the Day.<ref name="lobby1998">[http://www.decipher.com/ Welcome To Decipher!], Decipher (January 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980110221307/http://www.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>

=== 1999–2002: DECIPHER.com ===
In 1999 the site was redesigned as "DECIPHER.com", with a top bar linking each game, Help, About Decipher, Art Show, Tournaments, Message Boards, The Eccentric Order and the Party Zone.<ref name="sitemap1999">[http://decipher.com/sitemap.html DECIPHER.com: Site Map], Decipher (September 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991013075005/http://decipher.com/sitemap.html Internet Archive]</ref> Each game area had the same sub-sections: what is it?, rules, deck designs, card lists, strategy, fun and where to buy. In 2000 the home page listed ''Star Trek CCG'', ''Star Wars CCG'', ''Young Jedi CCG'' and ''Austin Powers CCG''.<ref name="home2000">[http://www.decipher.com/ Welcome to DECIPHER.com!], Decipher (March 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000301100924/http://www.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref> ''Jedi Knights TCG'' was added in 2001, along with Terms and Usage and Privacy Notice links.<ref name="home2001">[http://www.decipher.com/index.html Welcome To DECIPHER.com], Decipher (June 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010608101933/http://www.decipher.com/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> By March 2002 ''The Lord of the Rings'' led the navigation.<ref name="home2002">[http://www.decipher.com/ Welcome To DECIPHER.com], Decipher (March 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020329153115/http://www.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>

=== 2002–2005: Lord of the Rings and new games ===
From 2003 news moved to a <code>/content/</code> folder. The home page covered ''The Lord of the Rings'' TCG and RPG, ''Star Trek CCG'' Second Edition and RPG and the Party Zone. It linked to the online store, Decipher Online and the DGMA tournament site.<ref name="home2003">[http://www.decipher.com/ Welcome To DECIPHER.com], Decipher (January 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030122055529/http://www.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref> In 2004 it added ''.hack//ENEMY'', ''MegaMan NT Warrior'' and ''Beyblade''.<ref name="home2004">[http://www.decipher.com/ Welcome To DECIPHER.com], Decipher (January 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040123175015/http://www.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref> By January 2005 ''WARS TCG'' led the page and many links pointed to the fanhq.com domain.<ref name="home2005">[http://www.decipher.com/ Welcome To DECIPHER.com], Decipher (January 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050101091928/http://www.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>

=== 2005 onward ===
In April 2005 the home page began forwarding visitors to decipher.fanHQ.com, which lasted until early 2008.<ref name="fanhq">[http://www.decipher.com/ Welcome To DECIPHER.com], Decipher (April 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050406081350/http://www.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref> In April 2008 the address pointed to a ''Fight Klub'' blog, and in 2009 the home page announced ''Fight Klub'' with the line "Decipher reinvents the Trading Card Game".<ref name="fk2009">[http://decipher.com/ FightKlūb: Home], Decipher (January 2009). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20090119035440/http://decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref> From 2010 the home page was the ''Fight Klub'' site itself.<ref name="fk2010">[http://www.decipher.com/ Fight Klūb], Decipher (December 2010). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20101231224330/http://www.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref> Since 2014 the site has shown one page for ''How to Host a Murder''.<ref name="hthm2014">[http://www.decipher.com/ Decipher], Decipher (March 2014). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20140328135210/http://www.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref> As of 2026 it links to that line at Cryptozoic.<ref name="hthm2026">[http://www.decipher.com/ Decipher], Decipher (March 2026). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260307203616/http://www.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>

== Star Wars CCG section ==
From 1996 to 2001 the ''Star Wars CCG'' section was the largest part of the site. The Internet Archive holds about 227,000 unique URLs under decipher.com and its subdomains, about 19,000 of them under <code>/starwars/</code>, most of them one-page-per-card card lists.

=== Early pages (1996) ===
The first SWCCG pages were at <code>/swccg/</code> in 1996. They had card lists for Premiere, the Jedi Pack, ''A New Hope'' and Hoth (HTML and PDF), a rules FAQ released on 1 May 1996, Hoth rules, strategy and deck-design pages, a "card of the day" and links to Decipher's bulletin boards.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/swccg/cardlist.html SWCCG Card Lists], Decipher (1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961121231603/http://www.decipher.com:80/swccg/cardlist.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref>[http://www.decipher.com/swccg/faqs.html Frequently Asked Questions], Decipher (1 May 1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961121231546/http://www.decipher.com:80/swccg/faqs.html Internet Archive]</ref>

=== /starwars/ (1996–1999) ===
By December 1996 the game had its own home at <code>/starwars/</code>, with six areas: Product Library, Player Activities, Tournaments, Diversions, Bulletin Boards and the International Lounge.<ref>[http://games.decipher.com/starwars/index.html Welcome To Star Wars CCG!], Decipher (December 1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961231210522/http://games.decipher.com/starwars/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> By late 1998 the Bulletin Boards had become ''Dialog'' and a ''Special Events'' area had been added.<ref>[http://search.decipher.com/starwars/index.html Welcome To Star Wars Customizable Card Game!], Decipher (December 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19981202095514/http://search.decipher.com/starwars/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Product Library''' had set histories ("The Collection"), card lists, rules, FAQs, sample games, articles and deck designs.<ref>[http://games.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/index.html Product Library], Decipher (1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961231211115/http://games.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> Rules supplements were offered as PDF and HTML, with text and Word copies on Decipher's FTP server at <code>ftp://games.decipher.com/pub/SWCCG/</code>.<ref>[http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/index.html Rules], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327204812/http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/rules/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Player Activities''' presented the volunteer Rebel Squadron (see [[Decipher Squadrons]]), founded in 1996, which by 1997 had more than 90 members in Red and Gold Squadrons. It also profiled the two Rebel Leaders, Jonathan Quesenberry (Red 1) and Kendrick Summers (Gold 1), Decipher demo staff who toured stores and conventions.<ref>[http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/playeractivities/squadrons/index.html Squadrons], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327211728/http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/playeractivities/squadrons/index.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref>[http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/playeractivities/rebelleaders/index.html Rebel Leaders], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327211720/http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/playeractivities/rebelleaders/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> The area also had the player registry, a "Newbie Zone" and a where-to-buy list.
* '''Dialog''' linked the web bulletin boards (general, marketplace, tournament and others). It also hosted the '''Star Wars CCG Palace''', a graphical chat world on The Palace software at <code>palace://starwarsccg-palace.decipher.com</code>. Players downloaded Star Wars art and sound files to use there.<ref>[http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/dialog/index.html Dialog], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327205912/http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/dialog/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> The Palace opened with a party on 14 March 1997 with more than thirty rooms and more than two hundred guests.<ref>[http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/index.html Special Events], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327205534/http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> Dialog's listserv page offered Decipher's [[Decipher mailing lists|mailing lists]] and its faxback and email-back document services.<ref name="listserv1998">[http://search.decipher.com/starwars/dialog/listserv/index.html Dialog: Listserv], Decipher (December 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19981203075330/http://search.decipher.com/starwars/dialog/listserv/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Diversions''' had fan-designed "dream cards", top ten lists, "clippings" from players and "the attic" of retired pages.<ref>[http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/diversions/index.html Diversions], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327205903/http://rothko.decipher.com/starwars/diversions/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''International Lounge''' had pages for Europe, Japan, Australia and about a dozen European countries. In late 1998 only the Japanese Premiere and ''A New Hope'' editions were finished; German, Spanish, French and Italian versions were "in development".<ref>[http://search.decipher.com/starwars/internationallounge/index.html International Lounge], Decipher (December 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19981201190303/http://search.decipher.com/starwars/internationallounge/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> See [[Translations of SWCCG]].

=== Redesign (1999–2001) ===
In late 1999 the section was reorganized into What Is It, Card Lists, Rules, Strategy, Where to Buy, Star Wars Fun, Message Boards, Tournaments and Deck Designs, with product pages for each expansion under <code>/starwars/expansions/</code>.<ref>[http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/index.html Star Wars CCG], Decipher (March 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000302135655/http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Card Lists''' covered every set, newest first. Each set had Light Side and Dark Side HTML lists, a PDF and a plain-text version; newer sets also had spoiler and foil lists.<ref>[http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Card Lists], Decipher (April 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000409000000/http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Rules''' held the [[Decipher Rulebook 2.0|Rulebook 2.0]] and [[Decipher Glossary 2.0|Glossary 2.0]] (both November 1998), expansion rulesheets and the [[Decipher Current Rulings Document|Current Rulings Document]] as PDF and text. It also had an HTML "Combined Glossary & Current Rulings Document" last updated on 1 October 1999.<ref>[http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/rules/index.html Rules], Decipher (April 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000410045107/http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/rules/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Tournaments''' linked the World Championship finals, team events, Enhanced Premiere Pack sealed events and tournament-director tools.<ref>[http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/index.html Tournaments], Decipher (April 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000410155736/http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/tournaments/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> Tournament support later moved to tournaments.decipher.com.
* '''Deck Designs''' (see [[Decipher deck designs]]) listed player and staff decks by month, rated Beginner, Intermediate or Expert.<ref>[http://bbs.decipher.com/starwars/deckdesigns/index.html Star Wars CCG Deck Designs], Decipher (April 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000413160546/http://bbs.decipher.com/starwars/deckdesigns/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> '''Strategy''' carried beginner articles by Palace host "Landy" and "classic" articles by players.<ref>[http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/strategy/index.html Star Wars CCG Strategy Articles], Decipher (April 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000410125651/http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/strategy/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* A <code>/marajade/</code> promotion presented model [[Shannon Baksa]], cast in 1999 as [[Mara Jade]] for the Enhanced Jabba's Palace card.<ref>[http://calder.decipher.com/marajade/index.html Decipher Presents Mara Jade!], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001023003214/http://calder.decipher.com/marajade/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

=== End of the license ===
On 28 December 2001 a special [[Radio Free Decipher]] interview with chief executive [[Warren Holland]] announced that Lucasfilm would not renew Decipher's license (see [[Decipher and the Star Wars CCG Lucasfilm license|Decipher Lucasfilm license]]). It gave a manufacturing and sell-off period through 30 April 2002.<ref>[http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/rfd011228transcript.html Transcript of Radio Free Decipher Interview with Warren Holland], Decipher (28 December 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020305131228/http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/rfd011228transcript.html Internet Archive]</ref> An announcement page collected the audio, the transcript, excerpts from Decipher's July 2000 presentation to Lucasfilm, and contacts at Decipher and Lucas Licensing.<ref>[http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/announcement122801.html The Star Wars Announcement], Decipher (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020427144440/http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/announcement122801.html Internet Archive]</ref> On 25 January 2002 Decipher named the first Star Wars Player Advocates of the [[Players Committee]].<ref>[http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee1.html The Star Wars Players' Committee], Decipher (25 January 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020305131039/http://calder.decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee1.html Internet Archive]</ref> The Committee's [[Virtual Set 1: Legacy|Virtual Card Set #1]], twelve Premiere cards with new game text, was published on decipher.com as a PDF and became tournament-legal on 9 March 2002.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee/virtualcardset1.html Virtual Card Set #1 is Away!], Decipher (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020610072829/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee/virtualcardset1.html Internet Archive]</ref>

By 2003 the section's home page said Decipher had stopped publishing ''Star Wars CCG'', ''Young Jedi'' and ''Jedi Knights'' on 31 December 2001. It pointed players to the Players' Committee site, swccgpc.com.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Decipher (June 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030602173323/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> By 2005 it described itself as an archive of "selected web pages ... available for reference purposes" that Decipher was "unable to update".<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Decipher (September 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050903025429/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> Deck design, strategy and card-list pages were still online in 2006–2007, and the archive page until at least January 2008.<ref name="swarchive">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Decipher (January 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080129234445/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> By September 2011 the section returned "not found" errors (see [[Decipher after the Star Wars license]]).

== Other areas ==
* '''Inside Decipher''' (1996), later '''About Decipher''', had company philosophy, staff contacts and legal information.<ref name="inside">[http://www.decipher.com/insidedecipher/index.html Inside Decipher], Decipher (December 1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219004018/http://www.decipher.com/insidedecipher/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''West Wing / East Wing''' (1996–1999), later '''Party Zone''' (1999), covered ''How to Host a Murder'', Stir Crazy, Pente and Decipher's other party and family games.<ref name="partyzone">[http://decipher.com/partyzone/index.html Welcome To The Decipher Party Zone!], Decipher (March 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000304011330/http://decipher.com/partyzone/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Decipher Shop''' (1996) sent electronic postcards and sold promotional cards by mail; a full online store opened later at shop.decipher.com.
* '''Question of the Day''', '''Event Calendar''', '''Product Calendar''', '''Archives''' and a '''Volunteer Area''' appear in the 1999 site map.<ref name="sitemap1999" />

=== News ===
From 1996 to early 1999 news appeared under ''News and Highlights'' (<code>/newsandhighlights/</code>), as the ''Decipher NewsFlash'', with older stories moved to ''Inside Decipher'' archives and, from 1999, to <code>/archives/</code>.<ref name="newsflash1996">[http://www.decipher.com/newsandhighlights/index.html Decipher NewsFlash For November - December 1996], Decipher (December 1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219003928/http://www.decipher.com/newsandhighlights/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> From April 1999 to 2004 news ran under <code>/newsflash/</code>, and from 2003 to 2005 under <code>/content/</code>.

On 9 February 1998 Decipher announced an exclusive worldwide license for collectible card game rights to the Star Wars prequels. The deal also extended the ''Star Wars CCG'' license "into the next millennium". Holland said Decipher would use rights to ''Shadows of the Empire'', novels and computer games for CGI cards.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/newsandhighlights/swannouncement/index.htm The Future of Star Wars CCG], Decipher (9 February 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990508024221/http://www.decipher.com:80/newsandhighlights/swannouncement/index.htm Internet Archive]</ref> In February 1998 a ''Cloud City Month'' NewsFlash Special offered articles, deck designs, contests, live online games and Cloud City scenario tournaments run by [[Decipher Squadrons|Squadron]] members. First prize was a Cloud City poster signed by Jeremy Bulloch.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/newsandhighlights/cloudcityfeb/index.html NewsFlash Special: Cloud City Month], Decipher (February 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980130091907/http://www.decipher.com:80/newsandhighlights/cloudcityfeb/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> See also [[Cloud City Celebration]].

=== Galleries and Art Show ===
''The Galleries'' (<code>/thegalleries/</code>, 1996–1999) and its successor ''Art Show'' (<code>/artshow/</code>, 1999–2004) showed how "Decipher's studio artists make and present the art of the cards".<ref name="galleries">[http://www.decipher.com/thegalleries/index.html Welcome To The Galleries!], Decipher (December 1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219003948/http://www.decipher.com/thegalleries/index.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref>[http://www.decipher.com/artshow/index.html Art Show], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991013091417/http://www.decipher.com:80/artshow/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Future History''' showed prototype packaging for upcoming ''Star Wars CCG'' sets and the Parker Brothers two-player games, introduced by a letter from Warren Holland. The 1996 version announced Spanish, French, German, Italian and Portuguese editions.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/thegalleries/swccgfuturehistory/introduction.html Introduction from the CEO], Decipher (1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219010619/http://www.decipher.com:80/thegalleries/swccgfuturehistory/introduction.html Internet Archive]</ref> Its program page projected Hoth for November 1996, Dagobah for February 1997, Special Edition for June 1997, Bespin for October 1997, Tatooine for February 1998, Endor for June 1998 and Death Star for October 1998, and listed ''Shadows of the Empire'' as an expansion under consideration.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/thegalleries/swccgfuturehistory/theprogram.html The Full Program], Decipher (1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219040021/http://www.decipher.com:80/thegalleries/swccgfuturehistory/theprogram.html Internet Archive]</ref> It included two QuickTime movies and moved to Art Show as the ''Star Wars CCG Gallery'' in 1999, updated through the end of 1999.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/artshow/swgallery/index.html Art Show: Star Wars CCG Gallery], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991010002318/http://www.decipher.com:80/artshow/swgallery/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Easter Eggs''' had a page for each [[Easter eggs|Easter egg]] hidden in ''Star Wars CCG'' and ''Star Trek CCG'' card art. Decipher called them "fun little self-referential elements which we hide in the images and text of the cards".<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/thegalleries/eastereggs/index.html The Galleries: Easter Eggs], Decipher (1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219004408/http://www.decipher.com:80/thegalleries/eastereggs/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> By 1999 "all hidden eggs have been found".<ref name="eggs">[http://www.decipher.com/artshow/eastereggs/index.html Art Show: Easter Eggs], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991009143423/http://www.decipher.com:80/artshow/eastereggs/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''Creating Reality''' showed the studio's ship models for card art, such as the ''Hound's Tooth'', IG-2000, TIE Avenger, ''Punishing One'' and ''Mist Hunter''.
* '''NYC Showroom''' was a downloadable QuickTime VR tour of Decipher's New York Toy Fair showroom.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/artshow/nycshowroom/index.html Art Show: New York City Showroom Tour], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991009205220/http://www.decipher.com:80/artshow/nycshowroom/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Contests ===
The 1996 Hoth Contest posted a daily anagram of a preview card's title.<ref>[http://games.decipher.com/hothcontest/index.html Hoth Contest], Decipher (1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961102055122/http://games.decipher.com/hothcontest/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> The ''What's New'' area (<code>/new/</code>) ran the Decipher Easter Egg Hunt, with one egg hidden on the website each weekday from 21 to 31 March 1997.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/new/easteregghunt97/index.html The Decipher Easter Egg Hunt 1997], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327205157/http://www.decipher.com:80/new/easteregghunt97/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> It also ran the March 1997 Dagobah Contest, with five Shockwave puzzles,<ref>[http://rothko.decipher.com/new/dagobahcontest/index.html The Dagobah Contest], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327204942/http://rothko.decipher.com/new/dagobahcontest/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> and a Design a Card contest for Special Edition that closed on 14 April 1997.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/new/cardcontest/index.html Design a Card Contest!], Decipher (1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19981206081227/http://www.decipher.com:80/new/cardcontest/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> The Hoth Easter egg hunt closed on 19 December 1997 with two eggs never found.<ref>[http://decipher.com/insidedecipher/archives/1997/hothcontestcloses.html Hoth Easter Egg Contest Closes], Decipher (19 December 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990127105320/http://decipher.com/insidedecipher/archives/1997/hothcontestcloses.html Internet Archive]</ref> In 1999 an Endor "hidden cards" contest asked players to name five Endor cards hidden in forest artwork.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/product/1999/endor/hiddencards/index.html The DECIPHER Calendar: Spotlight – Hidden Endor cards], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990828214243/http://www.decipher.com:80/calendars/product/1999/endor/hiddencards/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

=== World Championship coverage ===
The ''DECIPHER Calendar'' (<code>/calendars/</code>, 1999–2002) carried the qualification rules for the [[1999 Decipher World Championship|1999 World Championships]].<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/worldchamps/index.html Welcome to the 1999 World Championships!], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991001003324/http://www.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/worldchamps/index.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref>[http://www.decipher.com/newsflash/swworldchampsdetails.html 1999 Star Wars CCG World Championship Details], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990508090740/http://www.decipher.com:80/newsflash/swworldchampsdetails.html Internet Archive]</ref> It also hosted the [[DecipherCon 1999]] site, with finalist pages and RealAudio play-by-play. In the final Gary Carman beat Steven Lewis.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/finalists.html Meet the 1999 Star Wars CCG World Championship Finalists], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991128125001/http://www.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/finalists.html Internet Archive]</ref>

The [[DecipherCon 2000]] site (<code>/deciphercon/2000/</code>) had a live camera, message boards, photos, reports and more than 20 RealAudio "Sound Bytes" interviews.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/index.html DecipherCon 2000], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001116205400/http://www.decipher.com:80/deciphercon/2000/index.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref>[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/soundbytes/index.html DecipherCon 2000: Sound Bytes], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001026143544/http://www.decipher.com:80/deciphercon/2000/soundbytes/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> Decipher streamed the championship finals as RealVideo in 20 kb and 80 kb versions. The ''Star Wars CCG'' final was the two-game match between [[Matt Sokol]] and [[Yannick Lapointe]], posted with both players' decks.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/finals/index.html Championship Finals Videos], Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001109002100/http://www.decipher.com:80/deciphercon/2000/finals/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

[[Radio Free Decipher]] (<code>/rfd/</code>, 1998–2003) was a RealAudio show, hosted in 1999 by Carol Wisely. It billed itself as "the authentic voice of Decipher's Young Jedi and Star Trek and Star Wars Customizable Card Games and the people who make them".<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/index.html Radio Free Decipher], Decipher (27 September 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991002050658/http://www.decipher.com:80/rfd/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Message boards ===
Decipher's first bulletin boards (<code>/bbs-master/</code>, 1996–1997) were threaded boards, including ''Star Wars CCG'' discussion (<code>swccg-bbs</code>), trading (<code>swccg-mkt-bbs</code>), tournament, "buzz", special and world boards.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/bbs-master/swccg-bbs.html Bulletin Boards: Star Wars CCG], Decipher (December 1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961219040702/http://www.decipher.com:80/bbs-master/swccg-bbs.html Internet Archive]</ref> About 1,500 pages of the SWCCG board survive in the Internet Archive. From 1999 the boards were CGI forums on calder.decipher.com, with discussion, trading, auction, off-topic and deck-design boards for each game.<ref name="boards1999">[http://decipher.com/messageboards/index.html DECIPHER.com: Message Boards], Decipher (September 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991008045136/http://decipher.com/messageboards/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> In 2004 they moved to phpBB forums at forums.decipher.com.<ref name="forums2004">[http://forums.decipher.com/ Message Boards :: Index], Decipher (June 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20040609100956/http://forums.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Volunteers ===
The <code>/volunteers/</code> area (1999–2009) listed [[Decipher Squadrons|Squadron]] tournament volunteers and Ambassadors by region. The ''Star Wars CCG'' regions were named after planets, such as Coruscant, Dagobah, Endor, Hoth: Ice Plains and Tatooine.

== Mailing lists ==
{{Hatnote|Main article: [[Decipher mailing lists]]}}
From 1996 Decipher ran e-mail lists through majordomo@decipher.com, including '''decipher-announce''', '''swccg-discussion''' and '''swccg-marketplace''', each with a digest version.<ref name="listserv1998" /> swccg-discussion, the main e-mail forum for the game, carried about 67,000 messages between January 1997 and December 1998.<ref name="egidx">[http://www.egroups.com/group/swccg-discussion/ swccg-discussion messages], eGroups (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991010033046/http://www.egroups.com:80/group/swccg-discussion/ Internet Archive]</ref> Around 2002 the lists moved to a GNU Mailman server at lists.decipher.com, whose archives were open only to members.<ref name="mm">[http://lists.decipher.com/mailman/listinfo/swccg-discussion Swccg-discussion Info Page], Decipher (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020612121031/http://lists.decipher.com:80/mailman/listinfo/swccg-discussion Internet Archive]</ref> The surviving messages are indexed on [[Decipher swccg-discussion list archive]].

== Downloads ==
Decipher.com offered a range of downloadable files for the ''Star Wars CCG'' and Decipher's other games: chat software, desktop wallpapers, QuickTime movies, Shockwave contest puzzles and RealAudio and RealMedia webcasts. It also offered printable card lists, rules and tournament forms in PDF and text format. Many of these files survive in the Internet Archive; the Palace chat installers do not.

== Subdomains and servers ==
* '''games.decipher.com''' was the first archived host (1996) and served the same pages as www.
* '''rothko''', '''christo''', '''dali''' and '''calder''' were servers named after artists. Calder ran the CGI programs, including the message boards and the e-card maker, and is the largest host in the archive, with about 65,000 URLs.<ref name="calder">[http://calder.decipher.com/ Enterprise Home Page], Decipher (December 1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19981205175446/http://calder.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''www1''', '''www2''', '''ftp''', '''bbs''', '''search''' and '''marajade''' served copies of the main site.<ref name="marajade">[http://marajade.decipher.com/ Welcome To DECIPHER.com], Decipher (April 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010420084813/http://marajade.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''starwarsccg-palace''' (1997–2000) hosted the Star Wars CCG Palace chat world; its web root served The Eccentric Order, Decipher's ordering site for the ''Star Trek CCG'' Fajo Collection.<ref name="eccentric">[http://starwarsccg-palace.decipher.com/ Welcome To The Eccentric Order!], Decipher (December 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19971222045757/http://starwarsccg-palace.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''startrekccg''' (2001) ran ''Star Trek CCG'' Online, built with DigitalDeck.<ref name="stccgonline">[http://startrekccg.decipher.com/ Decipher's Star Trek CCG Online], Decipher (February 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010202031300/http://startrekccg.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''tournaments''' (2001) ran the Decipher TCG Tournament System, with a tournament locator, player ratings and director logins.<ref name="tournaments">[http://tournaments.decipher.com/ Decipher TCG Tournaments], Decipher (November 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011112102743/http://tournaments.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''shop''' (2002) was The Decipher Store.<ref name="shop">[http://shop.decipher.com/ Welcome to The Decipher Store], Decipher (March 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020305223845/http://shop.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''info''' (2002) held files for distributors, magazines and translators.
* '''lists''' ran Decipher's Mailman [[Decipher mailing lists|mailing lists]].
* '''online''', '''lotrtcg''' and '''lotronline''' (2002) ran Decipher Online Gaming and ''The Lord of the Rings'' Online TCG.<ref name="online">[http://online.decipher.com/ Decipher Online Gaming], Decipher (November 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021129203047/http://online.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''rewards''' (2003) was a prize catalog priced in "Decipher Dollars".<ref name="rewards">[http://rewards.decipher.com/ Decipher for Prize Support], Decipher (October 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20031022210416/http://rewards.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* '''forums''', '''volunteers''' and '''retailers''' (2004) were community sites.
* '''reinvent''' (2007) was a teaser for ''Fight Klub''.<ref name="reinvent">[http://reinvent.decipher.com/ Happy Holidays!], Decipher (December 2007). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20071224071309/http://reinvent.decipher.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>
